title: Investigate intermittent GPU resident-set growth during continuous-batch KV hot-slice migration
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Production signals show intermittent steady growth in GPU resident memory (RSS) on servers running continuous batching with KV cache warmup. The growth is correlated with a specific traffic pattern where many short-context requests trigger repeated partial KV 'hot-slice' materialization and then partial eviction. We need to root-cause whether the allocator (cudaMallocAsync / mempool) is holding onto fragments, whether KV prefetching leaves pinned staging allocations, or whether stream synchronization barriers are preventing frees from releasing residency.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause hypothesis documented and validated with repro artifacts or eliminated
A mitigation implemented (config change, allocator tweak, or KV eviction fix) that stops steady RSS growth in the reproducible test
Perf dashboard: 7-day rollout showing no >5% regression in p50 latency or token throughput and stable RSS under the same traffic profile
Follow-up ticket(s) created for any longer-term allocator or runtime changes
repro_steps: Create a continuous-batching workload of short sequences (8-32 tokens) at medium QPS with synthetic KV keys: 80% hits but hot-slice accesses distributed across many keys
Enable advanced KV prefetching (prefetch: slice-level, staggered=true) and persistent pooling: staging_pool=enabled
Run for 4 hours with GPU resident sampling every 30s (nvidia-smi, perf counters) and track cudaMallocAsync call counts via profiling agent
Observe resident set growth and correlate to outstanding stream events and pending frees via runtime logs
Capture heap summary from mempool (if available) and collect stack traces for long-lived allocations
investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 — Initial triage: replicated growth in local stress cluster using same binary as prod. Growth slower than previous KV-prefetch incidents, but steady ~150MB/hour increase on T4-equivalent nodes.

2026-03-02 — Profiling: cudaMallocAsync allocation counts spike during warmup and then plateau; however resident bytes continue to climb. Observed pending frees sitting on non-default streams in runtime logs (stream ids 42/43 frequently).

2026-03-03 — Hypothesis A: frees are being enqueued to non-blocking streams and not observed by the CUDA async free background service due to stream lifetime / stream-quarantine timing causing delayed release back to pool.

2026-03-04 — Hypothesis B: KV partial-slice allocations are being promoted to pinned staging buffers for fast reuse but not returned to the LIFO slab due to slab-hysteresis thresholds tuned for large batches. The threshold prevents returning small fragments, increasing fragmentation over time.

2026-03-05 — Heap dump: mempool slab map shows many small resident chunks (~4-32KB) marked as staging in use=false but residency=true. Suggests unmap/unpin not happening even though CPU-side references were dropped.

2026-03-07 — Experiment: force stream synchronization at KV prefetch completion reduced accumulation rate by ~70% in the repro cluster, supporting Hypothesis A (stream sync delaying background unmap/frees).

2026-03-09 — Kernel-level check: observed kernel 'cuMemFreeAsync' returns queued, but eviction scheduler didn't drain because the quarantine window was set to 10s; repeated rapid prefetched staging caused quarantine to pile up. Lowering quarantine to 1s eliminated most of the observed residency growth in short runs.

2026-03-11 — Regression check: the quarantine window was increased in runtime-1.20 to reduce CPU/GPU thrash for large-batch workloads—this change explains why the issue surfaced with recent customer traffic skewing towards many small batches.

2026-03-12 — Conclusion: combination of (1) asynchronous frees tied to non-default streams + (2) conservative slab/quarantine thresholds that keep small staging fragments resident leads to gradual resident-size growth under continuous small-batch KV-hot-slice patterns.
mitigations_applied: Temporarily reverted quarantine window to 1s on canary hosts (config runtime.quarantine_window_s=1) — validated on canary cluster with negative RSS slope
Added an optional KV prefetch config 'staggered_prefetch=false' to reduce concurrent staging churn for customers running many short requests
Introduced runtime logging to emit 'pending_free_high_water_mark' events when pending frees > 1000 within 10s — for rapid detection
code_changes_and_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4298 — add configurable async-free quarantine window and runtime flag (WIP)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4310 — add diagnostic histogram for pending-free latencies to /metrics (merged)
https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache/pull/214 — optional staggered_prefetch toggle exposed in config (in review)
next_steps: Finalize PR 4298 with a safe default quarantine of 1s and a telemetry guardrail that flips quarantine back to 10s only when large-batch throughput and low fragmentation are detected
Roll the config change to 10% of hosts across regions for 48h, watch resident growth and p50 latency
Postmortem note and runbook: add check to detect continuous small-batch traffic patterns and auto-tune quarantine/prefetch settings
Follow-up long-term work: evaluate slab rebalancer that compacts small staging fragments into reusable LIFO buckets and improve stream-agnostic free draining logic (new ticket planned)
